args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (unhealthy, error rate 18% across us-east, us-west, eu-west). The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Next steps: confirm recovery and find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, was failing health checks and had an 18% error rate. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also unhealthy in staging before it went out.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the latest status check shows the service healthy with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged the on-call engineer. It says v2.3.1 failed after deploy, that it had already failed in staging, and that we rolled back to v2.3.0. It also lists next steps: confirm recovery and find the root cause before redeploying v2.3.1.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is the failing current deploy).
